# derived from monero v0.18.5.1 source, not captured from a run
# fields: COMMAND_RPC_TRANSFER's response is single_transfer_response,
#         src/wallet/wallet_rpc_server_commands_defs.h:567-594:
#           tx_hash string, tx_key string, amount u64,
#           amounts_by_dest = amounts_list (:556-565) -- the WRAPPER OBJECT { amounts: [u64] }, NOT a
#             bare array, and KV_SERIALIZE_OPT (:585) so it may be absent,
#           fee u64, weight u64, tx_blob string, tx_metadata string, multisig_txset string,
#           unsigned_txset string, spent_key_images = key_image_list (:547-554) = { key_images: [] }
# NO status/untrusted.
# FILE NAME: the wire method is `transfer`; the `-do-not-relay` suffix is a fmonero-mock SCENARIO
#         (--scenario do-not-relay). It is the DEFAULT build response all the same, because §2a.2
#         means fmonero NEVER calls transfer any other way: always
#         do_not_relay: true, get_tx_metadata: true, get_tx_key: false. The type makes the other
#         combination unrepresentable (§5b, WalletClient::build_transfer).
#         The mock also serves it for a bare `transfer` (transfer.json is a copy of this file), so a
#         test does not have to pass --scenario to exercise the ordinary build.
#
# `tx_metadata` IS WHAT relay_tx WANTS. `tx_blob` IS NOT. relay_tx's `hex` is the hex of a SERIALIZED
#   wallet2::pending_tx -- on_relay_tx parses it straight into a tools::wallet2::pending_tx
#   (src/wallet/wallet_rpc_server.cpp:1914-1943) -- which is exactly what transfer puts in
#   tx_metadata when get_tx_metadata is true. tx_blob is the WIRE TRANSACTION and relaying it fails.
#   The whole send flow of DESIGN.md §2a.3 rests on this: send::relay passes THIS response's
#   tx_metadata to relay_tx byte for byte, and a unit test asserts that identity.
#   The value here is plausible hex of the right shape, not a real serialized pending_tx: no mock can
#   produce one, and nothing in fmonero parses it. It is 512 hex characters, deliberately longer than
#   a txid so a test that mixes the two up fails on length alone.
#
# `tx_blob` IS EMPTY because the request sends get_tx_hex: false (KV_SERIALIZE_OPT false, :624), and
#   `tx_key` IS EMPTY because it sends get_tx_key: false (:622). Neither is KV_SERIALIZE_OPT on the
#   RESPONSE side (:583, :588), so both keys are present as empty strings rather than absent.
#   THE TRANSACTION SECRET KEY IS A SECRET (§2b.2): it must never reach --json, a log line, state.json
#   or DECISIONS.md, and fmonero never asks for it. An empty string here is the honest fixture.
#
# `fee` IS NON-ZERO AND IS THE FEE OF THE TRANSACTION THAT WAS ACTUALLY BUILT (§2a.2). fmonero never
#   estimates a fee, never multiplies get_fee_estimate.fee by anything, and never shows a fee it did
#   not receive from a built tx. 30720000 piconero = 0.00003072 XMR, consistent with
#   node/get_fee_estimate.json's 20000 per byte at priority 2 (80000/byte) over a 1531-weight
#   transaction of two inputs and two outputs -- plausible, not computed by any rule fmonero applies.
#
# `tx_hash` IS THE TXID THE WHOLE §2a CHAIN TURNS ON. It equals relay_tx.json's tx_hash (so the
#   §2a.9 comparison passes), get_transfer_by_txid.json's transfer.txid and get_transfers.json's
#   pending[0].txid (so the §2a.4 resolve step finds it). relay_tx-mismatch.json is the fixture that
#   makes them differ.
#
# `weight` 1531 matches node/get_transaction_pool_stats.json's bytes_med, i.e. an ordinary
#   two-in/two-out transaction. §5c's `wallet send` payload renders it as `weight`.
# `amount` 100000000000 = 0.1 XMR; amounts_by_dest carries the same single figure, because this build
#   has one destination. A sweep's counterpart is a LIST -- see sweep_all.json.
# multisig_txset and unsigned_txset are empty: multisig and cold signing are cut from v0.1 (§0).
# spent_key_images names the outputs this build selected. NOTHING MARKS THEM SPENT YET: on_transfer
#   calls commit_tx only when do_not_relay is FALSE (src/wallet/wallet_rpc_server.cpp:1213-1214), and
#   commit_tx is what sets them spent (wallet2.cpp:7628). That is precisely why a build reserves
#   nothing and §2a.11 needs the send.lock.
